rationale: EVT-0027 shows a failed network logon for 'hwalker' from wkstn-01 (10.0.2.89) to auth-srv-01 inside a continuous run of wkstn-01 auth and endpoint activity that, per fnd_fbf9c546485e, extends about 56409.3 seconds past that failure. The account 'hwalker' is otherwise active in the environment, driving an allowed cloud_storage access on meeting_notes_jun10.docx (EVT-0197). If the wkstn-01 sequence represents credential use that eventually succeeds rather than an isolated typo, the auth source that already carried EVT-0027, EVT-0049, EVT-0003, EVT-0012, EVT-0018 and EVT-0039 for this same source_host and dest_host should also carry a logon record naming 'hwalker' as the acting username with result 'success' to dest_host auth-srv-01 within that trailing window. If the auth source covers wkstn-01 through 2026-06-13T04:08:50Z (which fnd_bfb7effa55db and fnd_fbf9c546485e indicate it does, since later wkstn-01 records exist) and no such success record for 'hwalker' is present, that is an absence of the success rather than a blind spot, and the failed network logon stands as an unrepeated, unsuccessful attempt.

EVT-0192 shows 'dtaylor' from 10.0.1.16 acting on 'hr_policy_update.pdf' in bucket 'corp-documents', and the same file name recurs on EVT-0201 (~18415.4s later) and EVT-0213 (~24244.6s later). If those later touches are the same principal's sync client rather than a different account, the cloud_storage source should carry a record in that span with 'dtaylor' as the acting account on that file. If instead the cloud_storage records in that window name a different username, the same-principal reading fails; cloud_storage is the source that covers this, so an absence there is a real absence rather than a blind spot.

jclark is recorded accessing 'product_roadmap_v3.pptx' in bucket 'corp-documents' twice, at 2026-06-11T11:16:12.352464Z from 10.0.4.19 and at 2026-06-12T04:20:27.971638Z from 10.0.1.29 (fnd_fab2bd5da605, fnd_8e121e450d8d). A session that reaches cloud storage under that username should be preceded by an authentication for the same account; the auth source is the one that would carry it. If the auth source covers this period and holds no logon for jclark before these accesses, that is a finding about how the cloud access was obtained rather than about coverage.

EVT-0207 (fnd_170f88f97f02) shows the account 'asmith' performing an allowed cloud_storage access to 'client_proposal_acme.docx' from source_ip 10.0.1.16 at 2026-06-12T22:59:45.883199Z. The same address 10.0.1.16 is the dst_ip of the tcp flow EVT-0121 at 2026-06-12T12:02:46.441429Z (fnd_8a431658338b), which returned far more data than it sent and carries no account attribution. If the account 'asmith' was genuinely operating from the host at 10.0.1.16 during this period, the auth source should carry a logon record with 'asmith' as actor establishing that session at or before the cloud_storage access, falling between the flow to 10.0.1.16 and the file access from it. Absence of such a record in the auth source would mean either the cloud_storage session was carried over from an earlier session outside this window, or that the auth source does not cover this host - so if no auth events at all reference 10.0.1.16 or 'asmith', that is source blindness rather than a negative finding, and an endpoint/process_create record naming a host at 10.0.1.16 would be the alternative attribution path.

The username 'hwalker' fails a network logon from wkstn-08 to auth-srv-01 (EVT-0051) and later succeeds with a remote_interactive logon from wkstn-01 to auth-srv-02 (EVT-0039). If the same account is being driven across hosts rather than being two unrelated users, an auth source record should carry 'hwalker' as the acting username on a successful logon between those two timestamps - most plausibly on wkstn-01 among the uncharacterized auth records EVT-0049, EVT-0003, EVT-0012, EVT-0027 or EVT-0018, whose username and result fields are not yet read. The auth source is the only one that carries logon_type and result, so its silence here would mean absence rather than blindness; if no auth record in this window names 'hwalker' as actor, the two observations stand as disconnected uses of one name.

wkstn-10 is the single origin of a continuous run of logons under several usernames (dtaylor in EVT-0052/EVT-0028, hwalker in EVT-0019, ewhite in EVT-0048 and EVT-0016) and it is already covered by the endpoint source, which carries EVT-0174, EVT-0143, EVT-0189, EVT-0169, EVT-0145 and EVT-0188 on that same host. EVT-0048 establishes a successful interactive session for 'ewhite' from wkstn-10 at 2026-06-12T18:59:04.644060Z, and EVT-0016 records that same account failing an interactive logon from wkstn-10 to auth-srv-02 about 3802.7s later. If the run between those two auth records is one operator working from wkstn-10 rather than unrelated user activity, the interval between the successful ewhite session and the subsequent ewhite failure should contain at least one endpoint process_create on wkstn-10 with 'ewhite' as the acting account - the local work done inside that session before the next authentication attempt. If no such record is found, the endpoint source does cover wkstn-10 (as the listed endpoint events on that host show), so the absence would mean the session did no recorded process activity under that account rather than that the source was blind to it.

EVT-0196 shows 'fmartinez' repeatedly touching 'q2_budget_draft.xlsx' in bucket 'corp-documents' at the end of a chain of six accesses to that one file spanning roughly two and a half days, via a sync client user_agent 'OneDriveSyncClient/22.201'. If this repeated access is collection rather than incidental viewing, the cloud_storage source that already carries the view/access records should also carry an egress action - a file_download of that same file by 'fmartinez' - after the last observed access. The cloud_storage log is the only source that records bucket-level object actions, so if no such record is found there, that is an absence within a covered source rather than a blind spot; endpoint and network logs carry no account or file name for 10.0.3.14 in these findings and could not substitute.

The cited findings show wkstn-06 acting as the source_host for successful interactive and remote_interactive logons under four distinct usernames within roughly a day and a half - 'jclark' into auth-srv-02 (EVT-0021) and auth-srv-01 (EVT-0035), 'dtaylor' into auth-srv-02 (EVT-0056), 'glee' into auth-srv-01 (EVT-0057), plus 'iharris' owning the process_create EVT-0177 on the same host. One workstation driving logons to authentication servers under several different accounts is the pattern of credentials being tried from a single foothold rather than one user working normally, and such account cycling normally leaves at least one rejected attempt. If that reading is right, the auth source that already carries EVT-0021, EVT-0035, EVT-0056, EVT-0057, EVT-0058, EVT-0059 and EVT-0032 with wkstn-06 as source_host should also carry a failed_logon with wkstn-06 as the originating host, falling between the EVT-0177 execution at 2026-06-11T19:33:50Z and shortly after the EVT-0057 logon at 2026-06-13T02:22:03Z. If the auth source covers this window for wkstn-06 (which the cited successful logons establish it does) and no such failed_logon exists, the credential-cycling reading is weakened rather than merely unobserved, since the same source that recorded the successes would have recorded a failure.

If the outlook.exe -> chrome.exe lineage on wkstn-02 under 'dtaylor' (EVT-0149) represents a user following a link from a phishing message, the delivered payload should appear as a further process creation on the same host after that moment. The endpoint source already carries process_create records for wkstn-02, so it is the source that could see it; if no such record exists on wkstn-02 in the day following, the browser launch stands alone and the initial-access reading is not supported by execution follow-on.

EVT-0062 shows a single tcp flow from 10.0.5.26 (wkstn-03) to 10.0.2.20 on dst_port 53 moving 12779 bytes sent and 188372 bytes received - volumes far beyond a lookup exchange. Tunnelled or staged transfer over port 53 is not normally a one-shot event: if this flow is genuinely a covert channel rather than an isolated oddity, the network source that recorded EVT-0062 should also carry at least one further connection record with 10.0.5.26 as origin (again toward 10.0.2.20, plausibly again on dst_port 53 and allowed by the same outbound rule family) inside the surrounding span of wkstn-03 activity, which the cited finding anchors from the EVT-0002 logon about 10831.2s before EVT-0062 through the end of the dataset's observed activity at 2026-06-12T22:25:32.646863Z. The network log is the source that must decide this: it is the only cited source carrying src_ip/dst_port flow records, so if no additional 10.0.5.26-origin flow appears there, that is a true absence rather than a coverage gap, and it would argue EVT-0062 was a single transfer rather than a repeated channel.

A 2473829122-byte archive named 'backup_archive.zip' appears on host file-srv-02 under account 'jdavis' at 2026-06-10T16:51:03Z (EVT-0237) and the same byte count is uploaded at 2026-06-10T18:18:44Z from file-srv-02 (10.0.1.22) by 'jdavis' via user_agent 'python-requests/2.28.1' into the external-owned bucket 'ext-drop-xf9q2'. An archive of that size does not materialize without a process that built it, and the upload via a python-requests client implies a process executing on the host. If the staging-then-exfiltration reading is correct, the endpoint source that already recorded the file_create on file-srv-02 should also carry a process_create record on that host with 'jdavis' as the actor, at or before the file_create timestamp. I bound the window on the early side at the first observed intrusion-related activity in this dataset (2026-06-10T09:03:17Z, fnd_72d7e2b7f2cc) and on the late side at the moment the completed archive was recorded. If no such process_create exists, the distinguishing question is whether the endpoint source covers file-srv-02 for process_create events at all - it demonstrably covers file_create on that host - so an empty result there would be an absence rather than a blind spot.

EVT-0033 records a successful interactive logon for username 'cjohnson' from source_host 'wkstn-05' to dest_host 'auth-srv-01' at 2026-06-13T02:58:23.165329Z, and the same auth source that carried that logon also carries user_logoff events as a recognised event kind. A session that opens successfully should be closed by a corresponding logoff record naming 'cjohnson' as the acting account, following the logon in time. The auth source is the one that observed the logon for this account on this host pair, so it is the source that would have to carry the matching logoff; if the auth source shows no such record for 'cjohnson' after this timestamp, that is an absence within a covering source rather than a blind spot, and would indicate the session was never cleanly terminated in the window during which wkstn-05 activity otherwise ends.

EVT-0187 shows 'word.exe' spawned by 'explorer.exe' on host 'wkstn-02' under username 'asmith' at 2026-06-10T13:40:10.848419Z, which is the lineage of an interactive desktop session rather than a service context; an interactive shell session for that account must have been established on that host before the process was created, so the auth source should carry a successful logon record naming 'asmith' as the acting account with 'wkstn-02' as the destination host, dated at or before the process_create timestamp on the same day. The same account is already active in cloud_storage on 2026-06-10 (EVT-0199 at 12:18:41.520558Z), which places asmith's working session that morning. If the auth source covers wkstn-02 and no such logon record exists for asmith in this window, that argues the explorer.exe lineage arose from an already-open session begun outside the window; if the auth source carries no records for wkstn-02 at all, the absence is blindness rather than evidence.

Three findings describe a repeating beacon-like pattern from src_ip 10.0.1.13 (EVT-0110, EVT-0089, EVT-0073) and each cites a fourth record, EVT-0099, occurring between EVT-0089 and EVT-0073 (about 83223.5 seconds after EVT-0089 and 98984.5 seconds before EVT-0073). If the beaconing reading is right, that intervening record should itself be a network connection carrying 10.0.1.13 in the origin (src_ip) role, on the network source that carries the other three flows. If instead no network record places 10.0.1.13 as src_ip in that interval, the claimed four-flow series from this host does not hold.

On wkstn-01 the mail client 'outlook.exe' is recorded as the parent of both 'chrome.exe' (pid 3131, account iharris, 2026-06-13T04:07:27.113794Z) and 'explorer.exe' (pid 9691, account bwilliams, 2026-06-13T04:08:50.678413Z) within about ninety seconds. If those two process creations are the execution stage of a delivered payload rather than benign document handling, the payload has to reach an external endpoint to retrieve a stage or check in, which the network source should carry as a connection whose origin is wkstn-01 shortly after the second process creation. If the network source covers wkstn-01 in this interval and no such connection record exists, that weakens the reading of these two process creations as payload execution and favours reading them as ordinary mail-client-launched applications; if the network source does not cover wkstn-01 at all in this window, the absence says nothing either way and should be reported as coverage, not as a negative result.

wkstn-03 is repeatedly the source_host of authentication attempts against directory servers: a failed 'glee' remote_interactive logon (EVT-0054), a failed network logon for 'hwalker' to auth-srv-01 (EVT-0025 at 01:40:25), and then a successful remote_interactive logon for 'cjohnson' to auth-srv-02 (EVT-0002 at 02:59:42), with EVT-0053 sitting between them. If the reading that wkstn-03 is iterating accounts against auth servers until one succeeds is right, at least one further failed logon record with wkstn-03 as source_host should fall between the 'hwalker' failure and the 'cjohnson' success, carried by the auth source. If no such record exists in the auth log, which does cover wkstn-03 source_host fields, that would argue the success was not preceded by further guessing rather than that the source was blind to it.

fnd_2d5b74432030 reports that the 'psexesvc' service was deleted on host file-srv-02 under account 'jdavis' at 2026-06-10T20:05:38.000000Z. A service cannot be deleted unless it was first created on that host, so the same endpoint source that carried the service_delete record for file-srv-02 should also carry a service_create record for 'psexesvc' on file-srv-02 at some point before that deletion. The staging and upload activity tied to the same account and host (EVT-0237 at 11675 seconds before the deletion, EVT-0238 at 6414 seconds before, per fnd_2d5b74432030 and fnd_c29ab976709e) places the hands-on activity inside this same day, so the creation should fall in the window ending at the deletion timestamp. If the endpoint source covers file-srv-02 (which it demonstrably does, since it recorded both the file delete and the service delete there) and no service_create for 'psexesvc' exists in that window, that is a substantive gap rather than a coverage gap, and would mean the service was installed before the window or by a path this source did not record.

EVT-0195 shows cjohnson accessing 'q2_budget_draft.xlsx' in bucket 'corp-documents' from 10.0.5.11 at 2026-06-12T14:04:23.602351Z, part of a repeated series of touches on that one document by cjohnson, ewhite and glee. An authenticated cloud_storage access by a named username implies a preceding session established for that account, which the auth source should carry as a user_logon with cjohnson as actor before the access time. If the auth source covers these accounts and no such logon exists, that distinguishes a session not originating from an interactive authentication from the case where auth logging simply does not cover cloud_storage sessions; the cloud_storage records themselves carry no account-authentication detail, so only the auth source could show it.

EVT-0070 shows a single udp flow from 10.0.5.25 to 10.0.4.13 on dst_port 53 whose byte volume (28820 sent, 152845 received) is far larger than a normal name-resolution exchange, which is the shape of data carried over port 53 rather than a lookup. Tunnelled channels of that kind are not one-shot: the same source should appear as the origin of at least one further udp flow on port 53 after this one, within the period in which the other observed host activity runs (through 2026-06-12T17:10:30.174600Z, the latest timestamp in the findings). The network source is the one that carries these flows, and it already covered 10.0.5.25 at 2026-06-11T09:31:48.790384Z, so if no further flow from 10.0.5.25 appears in the network log inside this window that is a real absence rather than a gap in coverage, and it would argue the large transfer was a single isolated event rather than an ongoing channel.
